title: Air Fryer Picanha Recipe
ldIngredientsRaw: 3 pounds of whole picanha, fat cap on (also known as top sirloin cap, coulotte or rump cap )
1 tablespoon of a neutral oil (Something with a high smoke point like avocado, canola, or sunflower)
2 tablespoons of sal grosso (Brazilian coarse grilling salt), to taste (or any other coarse grilling salt)
¼ cup of unsalted butter, softened
1 tablespoon of fresh cilantro or parsley, minced
freshly ground black pepper to taste
ldInstructionsRaw: Take the 3 pounds of whole picanha, fat cap on, out of the fridge at least 1 hour before cooking so it isn't fridge-cold.

Make the herb butter: in a small bowl, mix the ¼ cup of unsalted butter, softened with 2 cloves of garlic, minced, 1 tablespoon of fresh chives, minced, and 1 tablespoon of fresh cilantro or parsley, minced. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Set aside.

Rub a thin layer of oil (1 tablespoon of a neutral oil) over the whole picanha, top and bottom, including the fat cap. Press 2 tablespoons of sal grosso (Brazilian coarse grilling salt), to taste, into the surface (press, don't rub, so the crystals grip).
Place the picanha in the basket fat side up and air fry for 10 minutes.
Flip fat side down and air fry another 10 minutes.
Transfer to a cutting board and cut into roughly 3 pieces. Salt the freshly cut sides to taste.
Arrange the pieces in the basket and air fry for 5 minutes.
Flip the pieces, work the herb butter into the meat, and air fry a final 5 minutes, or until they reach your preferred doneness. Pull the smaller tip piece earlier, since it cooks faster.
Remove each piece about 5°C (10°F) before your target temperature (see chart). Rest on a cutting board for 5 to 10 minutes, where carryover heat finishes the cook.
Slice against the grain and serve!
